---
title: "Clean Survey Data"
format: html
---

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
```

## Load raw data

Qualtrics CSV exports have three header rows:

1. Variable names (e.g. `v1_trust1`)
2. Full question text
3. Import IDs (JSON metadata)

We use row 1 as column names and skip all three header rows when reading the
responses. Row 2 is kept as a lookup table of question text.

```{r}
#| label: load-data

raw_path <- here::here("data", "data_raw.csv")

# Row 1 = column names, row 2 = question text
header <- read_csv(raw_path, n_max = 1, show_col_types = FALSE)

question_labels <- tibble(
  variable = names(header),
  question = as.character(header[1, ])
)

# Responses start after the three header rows
data_raw <- read_csv(
  raw_path,
  skip = 3,
  col_names = names(header),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

glimpse(data_raw)
```

## Remove metadata columns

Drop the Qualtrics metadata columns (timestamps, status, progress, language,
flow tracking, etc.). `ResponseId` is kept as a participant identifier.

```{r}
#| label: drop-metadata

data <- data_raw |>
  select(-c(
    StartDate:RecordedDate,
    DistributionChannel:`Last Seen Question IDs`
  ))

glimpse(data)
```

## Remove constant columns

Drop columns where every row has the same value (including all-`NA`), since
they carry no information.

```{r}
#| label: drop-constant

constant_cols <- data |>
  select(where(\(x) n_distinct(x) <= 1)) |>
  names()

# Report what will be dropped and the single value each column holds
tibble(
  column = constant_cols,
  value = map_chr(constant_cols, \(col) as.character(unique(data[[col]])))
)

data <- data |>
  select(-all_of(constant_cols))
```

## Composite scores

Each vignette (v1–v3) gets two composites, scored as the mean of 1–5 items:

- **Trust**: `trust1`–`trust5` plus `distrust1`–`distrust5`, with the distrust
  items reverse coded (6 − x) so higher = more trust.
- **Acceptance**: `accept1`–`accept4`.

Respondents missing any item in a scale get `NA` for that composite.
The single-item `satisfaction` measures are also converted to 1–5 (not part of
either composite) so they can be compared with the scores.

```{r}
#| label: composites

likert_levels <- c(
  "Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly agree"
)

data <- data |>
  mutate(
    across(
      matches("^v[1-3]_((accept|trust|distrust)\\d|satisfaction)$"),
      \(x) match(x, likert_levels)
    ),
    across(matches("^v[1-3]_distrust\\d$"), \(x) 6 - x)
  )

for (v in paste0("v", 1:3)) {
  data <- data |>
    mutate(
      "{v}_trust_score" := rowMeans(pick(matches(paste0("^", v, "_(trust|distrust)\\d$")))),
      "{v}_accept_score" := rowMeans(pick(matches(paste0("^", v, "_accept\\d$"))))
    )
}

data |>
  select(ResponseId, ends_with("_score"), ends_with("_satisfaction")) |>
  summary()
```

## Consent status

In each vignette, condition A asked for consent before MedHelper acted and
condition B only informed participants afterwards. Condition A contained two
consent requests (`reply1` and `reply2`); both are empty in condition B. Each
request gets its own status column: `{v}_status1` from `reply1` and
`{v}_status2` from `reply2`.

```{r}
#| label: consent-status

for (v in paste0("v", 1:3)) {
  cond <- paste0("cond_", v)

  for (k in 1:2) {
    reply <- paste0(v, "_reply", k)

    data <- data |>
      mutate(
        "{v}_status{k}" := case_when(
          .data[[cond]] == "B" ~ "Was not asked for consent",
          .data[[cond]] == "A" & str_starts(.data[[reply]], "Yes") ~ "Consented to MedHelper",
          .data[[cond]] == "A" & str_starts(.data[[reply]], "No") ~ "Did not consent to MedHelper"
        )
      )
  }
}

data |>
  select(matches("^v[1-3]_status[12]$")) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "status") |>
  count(column, status) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = n)

# Condition and replies are fully captured by the status columns
data <- data |>
  select(-starts_with("cond_"), -matches("^v[1-3]_reply[12]$"))
```

## Drop redundant columns

- `seq` is the A/B condition order across vignettes (e.g. `ABA`), which is
  already captured by the status columns.
- The individual `accept`, `trust` and `distrust` items are replaced by the
  composite scores. `satisfaction` is a single-item measure and is kept.

```{r}
#| label: drop-redundant

data <- data |>
  select(-seq, -matches("^v[1-3]_(accept|trust|distrust)\\d$"))
```

## Code field of study

`demo_field` is free text. `demo_field_cat` groups it into broad categories by
keyword. Rules are applied in order, so e.g. "Marketing (work) Clinical
Psychology (study)" is coded as Psychology. Non-answers ("None", "n/a", and a
comment about AI tools) are set to `NA`. The original text is kept.

```{r}
#| label: code-field

data <- data |>
  mutate(
    field_lower = str_to_lower(str_squish(demo_field)),
    demo_field_cat = case_when(
      is.na(field_lower) | field_lower %in% c("none", "n/a") ~ NA,
      str_starts(field_lower, "i have used these tools") ~ NA,
      str_detect(field_lower, "psych|dshb|human behavior") ~ "Psychology",
      # "engin" also catches the "Engineeing" typo
      str_detect(field_lower, "engin|\\bece\\b|computer|software") ~ "Engineering / CS",
      str_detect(
        field_lower,
        "epidemiology|public health|surgery|health services|speech|communication sciences"
      ) ~ "Health sciences",
      str_detect(field_lower, "biolog|biotech|animal") ~ "Life sciences",
      str_detect(field_lower, "sociolog|social work") ~ "Social sciences",
      str_detect(field_lower, "^art$|design|film") ~ "Arts & design",
      str_detect(field_lower, "retire|unemployed|disability") ~ "Not currently working",
      .default = "Other"
    ),
    .after = demo_field
  ) |>
  select(-field_lower)

data |>
  count(demo_field_cat, demo_field) |>
  arrange(demo_field_cat)
```

## Reorder columns

Identifiers first, then one block per vignette (consent status, outcome
measures, open-ended response), then the manipulation checks, and demographics
last.

```{r}
#| label: reorder-columns

vignette_cols <- map(paste0("v", 1:3), \(v) c(
  paste0(v, "_status", 1:2),
  paste0(v, c("_trust_score", "_accept_score", "_satisfaction", "_open"))
)) |>
  list_c()

data <- data |>
  select(
    ResponseId, consent,
    all_of(vignette_cols),
    paste0("check_v", 1:3),
    starts_with("demo_")
  )

glimpse(data)
```

## Save cleaned data

```{r}
#| label: save-data

write_csv(data, here::here("data", "data_clean.csv"), na = "")
```
